title: Spread of Christianity
summary: Word of Jesus's teachings spread to Jewish communities across the Roman Empire, helped by the empire's communications and by apostles such as Paul, who travelled around 10,000 miles over 30 years. At a meeting in Jerusalem about 49 CE it was decided that pagans could join without becoming Jews. By the end of the first century, these Gentile Christians dominated the movement.

uncertainty.note: The spread gathered momentum following the Apostolic Council in Jerusalem c. 49 CE and Paul's missionary travels in the 50s CE; it culminated in empire-wide legal recognition with the Edict of Milan in 313 CE.

as_recorded.value: spread of Christianity was made a lot easier by the efficiency of the Roman Empire

when.display: from c. 49 CE to the end of the first century

where.modern_name: Roman Empire; stand-in pin at Rome

importance.justification: The cross-cultural expansion of Christianity throughout the Roman world created the religious and institutional foundation of European and Near Eastern civilizations.

related.because: The spread of Christianity grew directly out of the initial community of Jesus's followers in Jerusalem.
Paul's missionary journeys across the Mediterranean and his epistles to Gentile communities drove early Christian growth.
The widespread expansion of Christian communities across the Roman Empire led Constantine and Licinius to grant legal toleration in 313 CE.

sources.title: Early Christians (The Roman Empire in the First Century)

reviewer_note: This outline covers only the first century. Later spread across other continents is not yet covered. The pin at Rome is a stand-in.
